pr_title: drivers: usb: fix stm32 USB clock configuration logic, enable USB on stm32f769i_disco

issue_context.title: STM32: support external ULPI PHY with OTG_HS
issue_context.body:
Followup to #12504.

**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
It is currently unclear whether the driver for the OTG_HS peripheral supports using an external ULPI PHY rather than the internal PHY. These ULPI PHYs are used on several ST dev boards such as the STM3240G-EVAL (from the original issue) or the STM32F769I-DISCOVERY (among probably many others); there is no way to use the on-board USB-OTG connectors with the internal PHY.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
If this setup is not yet supported, support should be added to the driver. If such support already exists, a sample should be added to demonstrate how it should be used, esp. regarding devicetree configuration.
comments: Hi, any update regarding this issue?

review_comments:
This modification will cause compilation error on the **STM32H747-Disco** Board  because it will compile a wrong condition and search for  the clock flag "**LL_AHB1_GRP1_PERIPH_OTGHSULP**"  that  was not defined  on stm32h7xx_ll_bus file  . 
To fix the problem, i think its better to modify the condition with
```c
#if USB_OTG_HS_ULPI_PHY && DT_HAS_COMPAT_STATUS_OKAY(st_stm32_usbphyc)

```

Aren't ULPI and PHYC incompatible with each other, and thus would never be active at the same time? My understanding is that there's either an external HS PHY connected via ULPI, or (on some models) an internal HS PHY called PHYC, or there's no HS PHY at all (FS only).

I also don't understand how `LL_AHB1_GRP1_PERIPH_OTGHSULPI` can be undefined, it's defined unconditionally in `stm32f7xx_ll_bus.h`: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/hal_stm32/blob/60c9634f61c697e1c310ec648d33529712806069/stm32cube/stm32f7xx/drivers/include/stm32f7xx_ll_bus.h#L100
Yes you're right it shouldn't be activated together, i guess on stm32h7 it should use another flag to enable the clock **LL_AHB1_GRP1_PERIPH_USB1OTGHSULPI**
Oh, sorry, I had misread "h7" as "f7" - yeah, h7 has a slightly different name for the define, I've fixed that now.
